(p-287) Surat al-Talaq

It is also called Surat al-Nisa' al-Qusra (the Shorter Sura of Women), and it is entirely Medinan by consensus of the scholars.

His Exalted saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: This is an address to the Prophet ﷺ, and the believers are included with him in it. Its meaning is: when you intend to divorce women, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When you rise to prayer﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 6]. There are two opinions concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse.

The first: it was revealed when "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced Hafsa, and he was told: Take her back, for she fasts often and prays often, and she is one of your wives in Paradise." This was related by Anas ibn Malik.

The second: it was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Umar, that "he divorced his wife while she was menstruating, (p-288) so the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to take her back, then keep her until she becomes pure." This was related by al-Suddi.

His Exalted saying ﴿for their waiting period﴾: that is, at the time of their waiting period, which is the state of purity (tuhr). This applies to a woman who has been consummated with, because a woman who has not been consummated with has no waiting period.

Divorce is of two kinds: sunni (in accordance with the Sunna) and bid'i (innovated).

The sunni divorce is that he divorces her in a state of purity in which he has not had intercourse with her. This is the divorce "for the waiting period," because she observes the waiting period by that purity, and the waiting period begins immediately after the divorce, so the period of waiting does not drag on for her.

The bid'i divorce is that it takes place during menstruation, or in a state of purity in which he has had intercourse with her. It takes effect, but its perpetrator is sinful. If he combines three divorces in one state of purity, then according to the preferred view in our school, it is an innovation (bid'a).

His Exalted saying: ﴿and count the waiting period﴾: that is, the duration of the waiting period. Counting it has benefits. Among them: observing the time for taking back (the wife), the time of maintenance and lodging, and distributing the divorces over the periods of acknowledgment if he wishes to divorce three times, and so that he knows she has become separated, so that he may marry her sister and four others besides her.

(p-289) His Exalted saying: ﴿and fear Allah, your Lord﴾: that is, do not disobey Him regarding what He has commanded you. ﴿Do not expel them from their houses﴾: this is evidence for the obligation of lodging. The houses are attributed to them because they resided in them before the divorce. It is not permissible for her to leave during her waiting period except for a clear necessity. If she leaves, she is sinful. ﴿Unless they commit a clear immorality﴾, and concerning this there are four opinions.

The first: the meaning is, unless they leave before the end of the period, and their leaving is then the manifest immorality. This is the view of Abdullah ibn Umar, al-Suddi, and Ibn al-Sa'ib.

The second: the immorality is fornication (zina). This was related by Mujahid from Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, Ikrima and al-Dahhak also said it. According to this, the meaning is: unless they commit fornication, so that they go out to have the prescribed punishment (hadd) carried out upon them.

The third: the immorality is that she becomes foul-tongued toward her family, so it is lawful for them to expel her. This was related by Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from Ibn Abbas.

The fourth: it is that she incurs a prescribed punishment, so she goes out for the punishment to be carried out upon her. This was said by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.

His Exalted saying: ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾: meaning what has been mentioned of the rulings. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah (p-290)﴾ which He has explained and commanded, ﴿has certainly wronged himself﴾: that is, he has sinned in what lies between him and Allah, Exalted is He. ﴿You know not, perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾: that is, He will place in the husband's heart the love to take her back after the first or second divorce. This indicates that what is preferred in divorce is to separate it (the pronouncements), and not to combine the three.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 65, verses 2–3:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then when they have reached their term﴾, meaning: they have come close to the end of the waiting period (ʿiddah). "Then retain them in an honorable manner." This is clarified in [al-Baqarah: 231]. "And call to witness two just men from among you." The exegetes said: call witnesses to the divorce or to the return (to the marriage, rajʿah). The scholars differed: is calling witnesses to the return obligatory or recommended? On this there are two narrations from Ahmad, and two opinions from al-Shafiʿi. Then He said to the witnesses: "And establish the testimony for Allah." That is: bear witness with the truth, and render it accurately, seeking the pleasure of Allah and fulfilling His command. What follows has already been explained [al-Baqarah: 232], up to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾. Most of the exegetes mentioned that it was revealed concerning ʿAwf ibn Malik al-Ashjaʿi, whose son was taken captive by the enemy. He mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ and complained to him of poverty. He said: "Fear Allah, be patient, and repeat frequently: there is no power and no strength except with Allah." The man did so, and the enemy became heedless of his son, so he drove off their sheep and brought them to his father; they were four thousand sheep. Then this verse was revealed.

Regarding its meaning, the exegetes have five opinions.

The first: "And whoever fears Allah, He will deliver him from every distress in this world and the Hereafter." This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: that his way out is his knowledge that what befalls him of giving or withholding is from Allah. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Masʿud.

The third: "And whoever fears Allah" by divorcing in accordance with the Sunnah and returning in accordance with the Sunnah, He will make for him a way out. This was said by al-Suddi.

The fourth: "And whoever fears Allah" by patience at the time of calamity, He will make for him a way out from the Fire to Paradise. This was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib.

The fifth: He will make for him a way out from the unlawful to the lawful. This was said by al-Zajjaj. The correct view is that this is general, for Allah, exalted is He, makes for the God-fearing a way out from everything that constricts him, while whoever does not fear Allah falls into every hardship. Al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym said: He makes for him a way out from everything that constricts people. ﴿And provides for him from where he does not expect﴾, meaning: from where he does not hope or anticipate. Al-Zajjaj said: It is also possible that it means: if he fears Allah in his divorce and conducts it according to the Sunnah, Allah will provide him with a wife in place of his wife. ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾, meaning: whoever trusts Him in what befalls him, Allah suffices him in what concerns him. ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose.﴾ Hafs and al-Mufaddal from ʿAsim recited ﴿bālighu amrihi﴾ with a genitive construction (idafah). The meaning: He executes what He wills. ﴿Indeed, Allah has set a decree for everything﴾, meaning: a term and a limit to which it arrives; Allah has determined all of that, so it is neither advanced nor delayed. Muqatil said: Allah has set for everything, of hardship and ease, a measure; He determined when this wealthy man becomes poor and this poor man becomes wealthy.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 65, verse 4–5:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation﴾. Regarding the occasion of its revelation there are two accounts. One of them: "When the ʿiddah (waiting period) of the divorced woman and of the widow was revealed in [al-Baqarah: 227, 232], Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: 'O Messenger of Allah, women of Madinah are saying: there remain among women those whom nothing has been mentioned about.' He said: 'And what are they?' He said: 'The young and the old, and those with child.' So this verse was revealed." This was narrated by ʿAmr ibn Salim.

The second: "When the saying of the Exalted was revealed: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228], Khallad ibn al-Nuʿman al-Ansari said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the ʿiddah of the one who does not menstruate, the ʿiddah of the one who has not yet menstruated, and the ʿiddah of the pregnant?' So this verse was revealed." This was related by Muqatil. The meaning of the verse: "If you are in doubt," i.e., you are uncertain and do not know what their ʿiddah is, "then their ʿiddah is three months, and those who have not menstruated [likewise]."

Section

Qadi Abu Yaʿla said: The intended meaning of doubt (irtiyab) here is the doubt of the addressees regarding the length of the ʿiddah of the postmenopausal and the young girl: how long is it? It does not mean the doubt of the women undergoing ʿiddah concerning despair of menstruation or despair of pregnancy, for the reason mentioned in the occasion of revelation. And because if the women were intended (p-294) by it, the address would have been directed to them, saying: "If you (fem.) doubt," since menstruation is known only from their side.

It has been disputed concerning a woman whose menstruation is delayed without a cause: how long does she remain in ʿiddah? The position of our companions (the Hanbalis) is that she waits for the usual period of pregnancy, which is nine months, and then three [months]. The ʿiddah is the three months that follow the nine. If she menstruates before the year by a day, she begins anew with three menstrual periods; and if the year is completed without menstruation, she is released (ḥallat). This is also the view of Malik. Abu Hanifa and al-Shafiʿi in his new opinion (al-jadid) said: she remains indefinitely until the cleanness of her womb is known with certainty, which is that she reaches an age in which women like her do not menstruate; after that she observes three months of ʿiddah.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾, meaning: their ʿiddah is also three months, because this is a clause that does not stand independently, so it must have a pronoun, and its pronoun has been mentioned explicitly, namely the ʿiddah in months. According to the view of our companions, this is applied to the one upon whom the time of menstruation has not come: she observes three months. As for the one upon whom the time of menstruation has come but who has not menstruated, she observes a year.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And for those with child, their term is that they lay down their burden﴾, is general concerning divorced women and widows whose husbands have died. This is the view of ʿUmar, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿud, Abu Masʿud al-Badri, Abu Hurayrah, and the jurists of the regions. It has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: she observes the later of the two terms. Our position is supported by the generality of the verse. And the saying of Ibn Masʿud: "Whoever wishes, I will curse him (in mubahala); ﴿and those with child﴾ was not revealed except after the verse of the widow," (p-295) and the saying of Umm Salamah: "Subay'ah gave birth a few days after her husband's death, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered her to marry."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾, i.e., in what He has commanded, ﴿He will make for him of his affair ease﴾, He will facilitate for him the affair of this world and the Hereafter. This is the view of most. Al-Dahhak said: "Whoever fears Allah in the divorce of the Sunnah, Allah will make for him of his affair ease in the return (to the wife)." ﴿That is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears Allah﴾ by obeying Him, ﴿He will remove from him his misdeeds﴾, i.e., He will erase his sins, ﴿and will magnify for him reward﴾ in the Hereafter.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 65, verse 6–7:

"Make them dwell where you dwell" (أسْكَنُوهُنَّ مِن حَيْثُ سَكَنْتُمْ). The "min" (مِن) is connected to his words "according to your means" (مِن وُجْدِكُمْ). (p-296) The majority of reciters read the "wa" (واو) with a damma (ضمة). Abu Hurayra, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, Abu Razin, Qatada, and Rawh from Ya'qub read it with a kasra (كسرة). Ibn Ya'mar, Ibn Abi 'Abla, and Abu Haywa read it with a fatha (فتحة). Ibn Qutayba said: that is, according to your capacity. Al-wujd (الوُجْد) means ability and wealth; it is said: "So-and-so became poor after having means." Al-Farra' said: He means: according to what one finds. If he is well-off, he widens for them in housing and maintenance; and if he is restricted, then according to that measure.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not harm them﴾ by constricting them in housing and maintenance, while you have abundance. Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la said: What is meant by this is the revocably divorced woman, not the irrevocably divorced one, by the evidence of His words: ﴿You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾ [At-Talaq: 1], and His words: ﴿Then when they have reached their term, either retain them according to acceptable terms or part with them according to acceptable terms﴾ [At-Talaq: 2]. This indicates that He intended the revocable divorcee.

The jurists have differed concerning the irrevocably divorced woman: does she have housing and maintenance during the period of 'idda (waiting period), or not? The well-known view among our companions is that she has neither housing nor maintenance, and this is the view of Ibn Abi Layla. Abu Hanifa said: she has housing and maintenance. Malik and al-Shafi'i said: she has housing but not maintenance. It was narrated by al-Kawsaj from Ahmad. The first view is supported by the hadith of Fatima bint Qays that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "Maintenance is only due to the wife from her husband as long as he has the right of return over her; but if he has no right of return over her, then there is no maintenance and no housing." And in terms of reasoning: maintenance is only obligatory in return for the wife's availability for sexual enjoyment, as is evident from the fact that a rebellious wife has no maintenance. (p-297) They differed regarding the pregnant woman and the woman whose husband has died. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Sha'bi, Shurayh, and Ibrahim said: her maintenance is from the entire estate, and this is the view of Malik, Ibn Abi Layla, and al-Thawri. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and 'Ata' said: her maintenance is from her own property, and this is the view of Abu Hanifa and his companions. Ahmad is reported to have held both views.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if they breastfeed for you, then give them their payment﴾, meaning: the wage for nursing. In this there is evidence that if the mother agrees to nurse him for the wage of his like, the father may not seek another woman to nurse him. ﴿And confer among yourselves in kindness﴾, meaning: the woman should not overreach the husband in what she asks for as wage for nursing, and the husband should not fall short of the amount due. ﴿And if you are in discord﴾ over the wage, and the two parents do not agree on something, ﴿then another woman will nurse for him﴾. The wording is that of a report, but its meaning is a command: that is, the father should seek a nurse other than the child's mother.

﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth﴾: He commanded those of abundance to widen upon their wives who are nursing their children according to their means. Ibn al-Sumayfa' read (لِيُنْفِقَ) with a fatha on the qaf (قاف). ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted﴾, meaning: constricted for him, from among the divorcees. Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Humayd read (قُدِّرَ) with a damma on the qaf and a shadda on the dal. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abi 'Abla read (قَدَّرَ) with a fatha on the qaf and a shadda on the dal, and (رِزْقَهُ) with a fatha on the qaf. ﴿Then let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾, according to the measure of what He has given him. ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾, meaning: according to the measure of the wealth He has given it. ﴿Allah will bring about, after hardship, ease﴾, meaning: after constriction and hardship, wealth and abundance. At that time poverty was predominant among them, so He informed them that He would open up provision for them after that.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Humayd read (قُدِّرَ) with a damma on the qaf and a shadda on the dal. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abi 'Abla read (قَدَّرَ) with a fatha on the qaf and a shadda on the dal, and (رِزْقَهُ) with a fatha on the qaf. ﴿Then let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾, according to the measure of what He has given him. ﴿Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it﴾, meaning: according to the measure of the wealth He has given it. ﴿Allah will bring about, after hardship, ease﴾, meaning: after constriction and hardship, wealth and abundance. At that time poverty was predominant among them, so He informed them that He would open up provision for them after that.

(p-298) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers﴾, that is: against the command of His messengers. The meaning is: its people became insolent. Ibn Zayd said: "ʿatat" means they disbelieved and abandoned the command of their Lord, so they did not accept it. Regarding the rest of the verse there are two opinions.

The first: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it. The meaning is: We punished them with a dreadful punishment in this world through hunger, the sword and calamities, and We called them to account with a severe reckoning in the Hereafter. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Farrāʾ, among others.

The second: that it stands in its own order, and the meaning is: We called them to account for their deeds in this world, and We requited them with punishment in proportion to their deeds. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and We punished them﴾, so He made the requital by punishment a reckoning. The severe reckoning is that which admits no pardon, and the "nukr" is the reprehensible. ﴿So they tasted the evil consequence of their affair﴾, that is, the recompense of their sin, ﴿and the outcome of their affair was loss﴾ in this world and the Hereafter. Ibn Qutaybah said: "al-khusr" means ruin.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah has sent down to you a reminder﴾, that is, the Qur'an. ﴿A messenger﴾, that is: and He sent him as a messenger, as Muqatil said. al-Suddi went in a similar direction. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: "the messenger" here is Jibril; in that case the reminder and the messenger are both sent down. Tha'lab said: "the messenger" is the reminder itself. Others said: the meaning of "the reminder" here is honor.

(p-299) As for what follows it, it has already been discussed (al-Baqarah: 257; al-Ahzab: 43; al-Taghabun: 9), up to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah has granted him a good provision﴾, meaning: Paradise, whose bounty never ends.

His saying, ﴿and of the earth the like of them﴾, means: and He created the earths in the same number as them.

A hadith states: "The thickness of each heaven is a five-hundred-year journey, and the distance between it and the next is likewise. The thickness of each earth is five hundred years, and the distance between it and the next earth is likewise."

Abu al-Duha narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "In every earth there is an Adam like your Adam, a Nuh like your Nuh, an Ibrahim like your Ibrahim, and an Isa like your Isa." This report is [sometimes] traced back to Ibn Abbas and [sometimes] stopped at Abu al-Duha. It has no meaning except what Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi related, saying: I heard that its meaning is that in every earth there is a kind of creation of Allah's creatures who have chiefs. Their eldest and foremost in creation stands in the position of Adam among us, and their descendants stand in age and antiquity in the position of Nuh. The rest follow this pattern.

Ka'b said: The inhabitant of the second earth is the barren sea. In the third are the stones of Hell. In the fourth is the brimstone of Hell. In the fifth are the serpents of Hell. In the sixth are the scorpions of Hell. In the seventh is Iblis.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿the command descends among them﴾. There are two views regarding "the command."

The first: it is Allah's decree (qada') and destiny (qadar). This is the view of most scholars. Qatadah said: In every earth of His earths and every heaven of His heavens there is a creation of His creation, a command of His command, and a decree of His decrees.

The second: it is the revelation (wahy). This was said by Muqatil.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿so that you may know that Allah has power over all things, and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾. He informed you of this so that you would know His power over all things and His knowledge of all things.
